page.overview:
Who is Zeus?

Zeus (Greek: Δίας & Ζευς) (Ancient Greek: Ζεύς, Ζεῦ, Διός & Διί) is the King of the Olympian gods and God of the Sky, Weather, Thunderstorms, Lightning bolts, Winds and Clouds. He is also the God of Law, Order, Justice, Power, Human Fate, and the Human Race. Zeus is called the “Father of the Gods” and “King of all”. His symbols are the thunderbolt, eagle, bull, and oak tree. His Roman name is Jupiter, or alternatively Jove. (Latin: Iuppiter & Iovis)

Zeus was the third son and sixth child of Kronos & Rhea. His other full siblings had been eaten by Kronos as soon as they were born (Kronos had been hoping to avoid one of them overthrowing him), however, Rhea gave birth to Zeus in a cave on Mount Ida in Crete, where she hid him from his father. The Kouretes & Daktyloi were three, five, or nine rustic Daimones (Spirits) appointed by Rhea to guard the infant Zeus, in order to keep him safely hidden from his cannibalistic father, the Titan (Stretching—God) Kronos, they drowned out his cries with a frenzied dance of clashing spears and shields. Meanwhile, Rhea gave a boulder wrapped in blankets to Kronos, who ate that instead, believing it was Zeus.

When Zeus came of age, he entered the service of his father, becoming his cup bearer. After gaining Kronos’ trust he eventually served him a mixture of mustard and wine, which made Kronos ill and caused him to vomit up the five children he had eaten and a rock wrapped in blankets. Not long after, Zeus allied himself with his siblings, the three male siblings went to Tartarus, where they convinced the Elder Cyclopes to make them weapons. The three forged the Helm of Darkness for Hades, a Trident for Poseidon and the Lightning Bolt for Zeus. The Elder Cyclopes and the Hekatonkheires helped build the palace on Mount Olympus and built weapons for the Olympians.

Zeus then—killed Kampe (the dragon lady who had been acting as the jailer for the Elder Cyclopes and the Hekatonkheires) Zeus freed—the Elder Cyclopes and the Hekatonkheires recruiting them for battle. A ten-year war erupted between the Titans and their allies and the Olympians and theirs’. Iapetos, Koios, Krios and Hyperion were imprisoned in Tartarus, Kronos was thrown into Tartarus, Atlas was cursed to hold up the sky, and Menoitios was struck down by a thunderbolt from Zeus and thrown into Erebos. As for the palace at Mount Othrys, it was buried beneath hundreds of boulders thrown by the Hekatonkheires.

Iapetos, Koios, Krios and Hyperion were imprisoned in Tartarus, Kronos was thrown into Tartarus, Atlas was cursed to hold up the sky, and Menoitios was struck down by a thunderbolt from Zeus and thrown into Erebos. As for the palace at Mount Othrys, it was buried beneath hundreds of boulders thrown by the Hekatonkheires.
